answer: An identity registers only with a Walnut credential: one non-transferable credential bound to one funding source, backed by a 500-token bond locked 90 days and slashed 100% on proven duplication. A public nullifier registry records each credential as a basalt-hard entry that cannot be split or reused, so a second registration is provably the same actor. Identities sharing one funder sit on the same ridge: on the third duplicate reveal, every identity on that ridge freezes and its bond burns. 1,000 fakes cost 500,000 tokens upfront, locked and unrecoverable, auditable by anyone in seconds.
